# ethereum-optimism/ecosystem Weekly Report (Aug 9 - 15, 2026)

## 🚀 Highlights
This week focused heavily on the long-term sustainability and technical debt management of the Optimism Interop ecosystem. A major initiative was launched to consolidate and clean up public developer-facing repositories, aiming to streamline the developer experience by archiving stale code and refining the scope of the `ecosystem` repository. Significant progress was also made in validating the performance of the Superchain Dependency Manager (SDM), confirming substantial gas savings without introducing builder overhead. While infrastructure monitoring saw improvements, the team is currently addressing a critical blocking issue in the `op-interop-filter` RPC that impacts transaction rejection speeds.

## 🛠️ Key Developments
While no new features were merged during this reporting period, the technical focus remained on benchmarking and infrastructure verification to ensure the stability of the OP Stack.

### SDM Performance & Monitoring
The team completed a comprehensive verification of the Superchain Dependency Manager (SDM) on `sdm-net-0`. 
*   **Benchmarking:** Re-runs of baseline benchmarks confirmed that SDM provides significant gas refunds to users while maintaining zero measurable overhead for builders ([#22344](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ecosystem/issues/22344)).
*   **Observability:** SDM dashboards were successfully migrated and verified within OPE Grafana, ensuring better visibility into the system's health, despite minor pending fixes for two empty panels ([#22345](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ecosystem/issues/22345)).

### Kona Node Testing
The team finalized testing parameters for the Kona node. It was determined that `TestSyncAfterInitialELSync` will not be supported in Kona, leading to the closure of the associated acceptance test issue ([#22278](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ecosystem/issues/22278)).

## 🐛 Issues & Triage

### New & Active Issues: Interop Repository Cleanup
A significant new epic ([#1008](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ecosystem/issues/1008)) was initiated to overhaul the public Interop developer environment. This effort includes several critical sub-tasks:
*   **Consolidation:** Moving disparate starter examples into a single, unified repository ([#1015](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ecosystem/issues/1015)) and refining the `ecosystem` repo to focus specifically on `viem` and `wagmi` packages ([#1011](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ecosystem/issues/1011)).
*   **Deprecation & Archiving:** Identifying abandoned repositories for a "2024 archive sweep" ([#1017](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ecosystem/issues/1017)), removing superseded relayer code ([#1010](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ecosystem/issues/1010)), and evaluating the future of `super-cli` ([#1012](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ecosystem/issues/1012)).
*   **Dependency Management:** Resolving stale Solidity dependencies in `interop-lib` ([#1009](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ecosystem/issues/1009)) and upgrading `supersim` to the latest OP Stack version ([#1013](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ecosystem/issues/1013)).

### Technical Blockers
A high-priority defect in `op-interop-filter` ([#21943](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ecosystem/issues/21943)) remains active. The verdict RPC is currently blocking behind an ingester write lock, causing transaction timeouts rather than immediate rejections. This was recently observed during testing with fabricated access-list keys, highlighting the need for a fix to prevent fail-closed timeouts.

## 💬 Community & Collaboration
The week was characterized by rigorous internal auditing and architectural decision-making. The cleanup epic ([#1008](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ecosystem/issues/1008)) indicates a collaborative effort to reduce friction for external contributors by removing "dead" code and clarifying repository scopes. Technical discussions around the `op-interop-filter` defect show active monitoring and debugging, with detailed reports on transaction failure modes helping to pinpoint the lock contention issues.
